The most substantive assessment of policing and justice-chain capacity by state and county describes case management, police staffing and infrastructure gaps outside Juba, and records for one state that Wau remains the only county with a functional formal justice system ([assessment](2022-01-01-undp-access-justice-security-human-rights-annual-report)).

No case management system, procurement for one, or plan naming one appears in the base. The absence is dated and cited rather than unexamined.

summary: A [state-level digital land registration framework](2026-07-08-central-equatoria-digital-land-registration-advance) is being built in Central Equatoria, against records the government itself calls handwritten.
developments:
The government's own draft land policy describes land administration as weak and largely manual, records often handwritten and formal administration concentrated in a few urban centres, and sets a National Land Registry and Land Records System as a policy objective ([policy](2023-04-23-draft-national-land-policy-south-sudan)).

Central Equatoria State's information ministry, with the state housing and lands ministry and county authorities, is developing a unified digital land registration framework beginning with land records in Juba County ([framework](2026-07-08-central-equatoria-digital-land-registration-advance)); a European Union and migration agency programme running in Rubkona and Yei River counties from 1 January 2026 commits to advancing the digitalisation of land records ([programme](2026-02-20-eu-iom-catalysing-durable-solutions-land-records)).

Three efforts in three places, none of them national, and the national registry the policy calls for does not exist.

summary: ***Not held***, searched 2026-09-06 - the [capacity assessment](2021-04-01-csps-undp-local-government-capacity-assessment) covering all ten states finds the institutions short of the basics.
developments:
The assessment covers organisational structures, staffing, infrastructure and working environment across the ten states and three administrative areas, and finds gaps across them ([assessment](2021-04-01-csps-undp-local-government-capacity-assessment)).

The one thing reaching sub-national institutions in the period is a national alerting roadmap for warning dissemination ([roadmap](2026-05-04-nca-ew4all-common-alerting-protocol)).

No state or county digital service platform is recorded, and the most recent assessment of what these institutions can run is five years old.

summary: [Central Equatoria is developing a unified digital land registration framework](2026-07-08-central-equatoria-digital-land-registration-advance), the first sub-national records digitisation in the base.
developments:
The state information ministry, the state housing and lands ministry and county authorities are building the framework, beginning with land records in Juba County ([framework](2026-07-08-central-equatoria-digital-land-registration-advance)).

A European Union and migration agency programme running in Rubkona and Yei River counties from 1 January 2026 commits to strengthening land governance systems and advancing the digitalisation of land records ([programme](2026-02-20-eu-iom-catalysing-durable-solutions-land-records)), against a national policy describing records as often handwritten ([policy](2023-04-23-draft-national-land-policy-south-sudan)).

Land is the only record class being digitised at this level. No council register, permit system or revenue record appears.

summary: The [first patient-level electronic register](2026-04-24-icap-first-electronic-art-register-south-sudan) went into use across five facilities, cutting missed appointments from 58 per cent to 11 per cent.
developments:
The register moved into operational use across five facilities including state hospitals at Rumbek, Yirol and Yambio, with more than 12,700 legacy records digitised and missed appointments falling from 58 per cent to 11 per cent between May 2025 and February 2026 ([register](2026-04-24-icap-first-electronic-art-register-south-sudan)).

An offline-first tracker on Android devices ran a twelve-month pilot for community health workers in remote settings, replacing paper household visit, childhood-illness and immunisation follow-up reporting ([tracker](2026-04-20-dhis2-boma-health-worker-tracker-pilot)).

Five facilities and one pilot, in a system where 22.4 per cent of facilities hold comprehensive electronic systems ([assessment](2025-02-01-who-his-maturity-assessment-south-sudan)).

summary: School reporting is [still largely manual with inadequate connectivity in rural areas](2026-03-24-au-iped-emis-reform-costed-action-plan), against a census already collected on tablets.
developments:
The annual education census collects school-level data on tablets into a web repository, covering enrolment, teachers, facilities and the availability of ICT teachers at schools nationally ([census](2023-01-01-mogei-national-education-census-report-2023)).

A three-day workshop in March 2026 documented school-level reporting as still largely manual with inadequate infrastructure and connectivity especially in rural and hard-to-reach areas, and produced a costed national action plan in response ([plan](2026-03-24-au-iped-emis-reform-costed-action-plan)); 84 computers, 33 motorbikes and one vehicle were handed to the education ministry in November 2025 to strengthen monitoring and supervision ([handover](2025-11-05-mogei-tess-equipment-handover-unicef)).

An annual census on tablets and daily reporting on paper is the gap the plan prices.

summary: [2,500 identity cards registered across the greater Yei region](2026-04-10-immigration-officers-registration-drive-yei-river-county), from an office that lacks premises.
developments:
An immigration directorate delegation to Yei River County reported 2,500 national identity cards registered across the greater Yei region to date, while recording that the county's own immigration office still lacks adequate and well-known premises ([visit](2026-04-10-immigration-officers-registration-drive-yei-river-county)).

Mobile registration kits were deployed from April 2026 ([kits](2026-04-25-mobile-registration-kits-deployed)), and distribution of more than 4,000 processed cards and passports began across the four counties of Greater Yei in July ([distribution](2026-07-10-yei-nationality-cards-distribution)).

Registration is reaching the counties by kit and by visit rather than through an office that can hold it.

summary: [Fifteen officers were trained on donated forensic equipment](2026-06-17-police-forensic-lab-equipment-china-training) and tasked with training others in the states.
developments:
Digital forensic laboratory equipment was donated with electronic fingerprint technology planned for a second phase, and fifteen officers trained and tasked with training additional personnel in the states ([equipment](2026-06-17-police-forensic-lab-equipment-china-training)).

A separately funded surveillance project was approved with a first phase limited to Juba and a stated second phase to expand across the country ([project](2026-02-08-smart-city-surveillance-police-plan)), against an assessment describing case management, staffing and infrastructure gaps outside the capital ([assessment](2022-01-01-undp-access-justice-security-human-rights-annual-report)).

No county station is confirmed to hold any equipment, and no station-level count exists.

summary: The ministry's own position is that [infrastructure, data centres and trained people come first](2025-04-03-moictps-outlines-three-pillars-to-properly-reap-artificial-intelligence); the one deployment is a public e-learning platform.
developments:
Speaking at a regional summit, the ministry set out three pillars - infrastructure, data centres and trained human resources - as prerequisites, and described no operational system in administration, only planned donor-funded training and fibre groundwork ([pillars](2025-04-03-moictps-outlines-three-pillars-to-properly-reap-artificial-intelligence)).

A national e-learning platform launched in June 2026 by the mobile operator with an education organisation and two ministries, zero-rated on that operator's network and carrying artificial-intelligence-supported content ([platform](2026-06-29-data-free-junub-academy-brings-ai-supported-education-to-south-sudan)).

A government-partnered public service, not an internal administration system. Nothing inside government runs on it.

summary: Two algorithmic systems run in production - a [malaria prediction pilot inside the national health instance](2026-07-01-south-sudan-dhis2-climate-and-health-country-profile) and a [monthly food security model](2026-07-06-south-sudan-joint-food-security-monitor).
developments:
A custom dashboard began piloting climate-informed predictive modelling and automated malaria outbreak alerts inside the national health instance in July 2026 ([dashboard](2026-07-01-south-sudan-dhis2-climate-and-health-country-profile)).

The food security monitor is a monthly sub-national early warning system combining conflict, price, climate and exchange-rate data through calibrated transformations and a weighted generalised linear model to raise alerts and estimate populations at risk across the 78 second-level administrative areas ([monitor](2026-07-06-south-sudan-joint-food-security-monitor)).

Both are built and run by external partners on donor systems. Neither is owned by the ministry whose sector it covers.

summary: No national strategy: the country [adopted the regional AI declaration](2026-04-09-eac-adopts-ai-declaration-resolving-to-establish-regional-ai-fund-and-prioritise-ai-sovereignty) and the [regional strategy went to validation](2026-05-05-east-african-community-advances-regional-ai-agenda-with-high-level-strategy-validation-workshop).
developments:
The ministry stated in 2024 that the country was working on establishing its own roadmap alongside other African states ([roadmap](2024-01-01-ministers-agree-on-ai-initiative-for-african-digital-transformation)).

As one of eight partner states the country adopted the East African Community Declaration on Artificial Intelligence at a regional conference over 30 March to 1 April 2026, committing to a regional fund, shared infrastructure, harmonised curricula and integration of artificial intelligence into development planning ([declaration](2026-04-09-eac-adopts-ai-declaration-resolving-to-establish-regional-ai-fund-and-prioritise-ai-sovereignty)); the draft regional strategy for 2026 to 2031 went to a two-day validation workshop in Kampala on 4 and 5 May 2026 ([strategy](2026-05-05-east-african-community-advances-regional-ai-agenda-with-high-level-strategy-validation-workshop)).

The national position is entirely carried by regional instruments.

summary: A [national cyber-security task force](2026-07-17-south-sudan-activates-cybercrime-law-to-protect-digital-space-ahead-of-elections) was stood up in July 2026 to enforce a statute with no AI provision.
developments:
The Cybercrime and Computer Misuse Act 2026, signed on 18 February 2026 and enforceable on signature, is technology-neutral - hacking, identity theft, cyberstalking, cyberbullying, false or misleading information - with no artificial-intelligence or deepfake provision ([explainer](2026-03-18-explainer-cybercrime-and-computer-misuse-act-2026-chapter-i)).

The justice minister publicly dismissed a circulating investigation report as an artificial-intelligence fabrication and warned of prosecution for creating or sharing it ([case](2026-04-27-justice-minister-dismisses-leaked-probe-report-as-fake-ai-fabrication-warns-of-prosecution)), and under a presidential directive a multi-agency task force and steering committee held its first operational meeting on 16 July 2026 to enforce the Act ahead of the December elections, including against false and misleading information ([task force](2026-07-17-south-sudan-activates-cybercrime-law-to-protect-digital-space-ahead-of-elections)).

A general offence of false information, enforced by a task force, in an election year.

summary: [No domestic hardware base](2022-06-01-south-sudan-digital-economy-assessment) and a nascent software sector, against a [2,400 kilometre fibre backbone](2025-10-08-constructions-of-countrys-fiber-optic-cable-begins-december) announced for construction.
developments:
The country diagnostic documents a nascent digital business sector - ride-sharing, information technology support firms, technology-enabled agribusiness - with no domestic hardware manufacturing base, severe skills and infrastructure gaps and no national fibre backbone ([diagnostic](2022-06-01-south-sudan-digital-economy-assessment)).

Construction of a 2,400 kilometre national backbone reaching the Indian Ocean through Kenya was announced to begin in December 2025 ([backbone](2025-10-08-constructions-of-countrys-fiber-optic-cable-begins-december)), and a Juba-headquartered company launched a multi-currency payments application in March 2026 ([application](2026-03-30-sarafa-is-now-live-on-the-app-store)).

One application on an app store is the base's clearest instance of domestic software production.

summary: A [four-year incubator for 350 small enterprises](2026-04-29-grebi-project-launched-to-drive-inclusive-agribusiness-growth-in-south-sudan) launched in April 2026, above a pitch competition that awarded EUR 90,000.
developments:
A pitch competition in Juba on 26 September 2025 saw 24 entrepreneurs compete and seven share EUR 90,000 in grants ([competition](2025-10-07-orange-corners-entrepreneurs-challenge-2025-inspiring-innovation-in-south-sudan)).

A European Union-funded incubator running 2026 to 2029 launched on 16 April 2026 at the University of Juba, targeting incubation, acceleration and finance for 350 small and medium enterprises across seven regions, 30 per cent women-led and more than half youth-led ([incubator](2026-04-29-grebi-project-launched-to-drive-inclusive-agribusiness-growth-in-south-sudan)).

Both are donor-financed and neither reports a company formed, funded or grown beyond its own cohort.

summary: Digital literacy was [found low but never measured](2023-01-11-eastern-africa-regional-digital-integration-project-stakeholder-engagement-plan); [three skills centres](2026-08-03-disk-programme-central-equatoria-digital-skills) are under renovation.
developments:
Stakeholder consultations found digital literacy low but did not tabulate it, there being no national statistics or third-party surveys, and the project responded by planning a competency framework and learning programmes for civil servants and university students ([consultations](2023-01-11-eastern-africa-regional-digital-integration-project-stakeholder-engagement-plan)).

Renovation began in August 2026 on three government facilities designated as digital skills centres in Central Equatoria under a five-year programme reaching more than 8,000 people including 3,000 civil servants ([centres](2026-08-03-disk-programme-central-equatoria-digital-skills)), and four ministry staff completed a public-service digital expansion programme in Wuhan ([training](2026-06-29-ict-ministry-staff-china-digital-training)).

Three years after the finding, the measurement still does not exist.

progress: No change, a first count with no earlier figure behind it
summary: No national measure exists and [one has been commissioned](2026-06-25-expression-of-interest-for-conducting-national-digital-skills-assessment-framework-development-and-implementation-plan); the best evidence is a [four-site household assessment](2026-06-22-digital-access-and-connectivity-in-south-sudan-barriers-for-refugees-and-host-communities).
developments:
A 2,135-household connectivity needs and usage assessment across four refugee-hosting locations, run between 15 January and 26 February 2026, found 72 per cent of respondents aware of the internet, 66 per cent of internet users unable to use it as much as they would like on grounds of cost, devices and literacy, and 41 per cent of women and 20 per cent of men unable to read and write ([assessment](2026-06-22-digital-access-and-connectivity-in-south-sudan-barriers-for-refugees-and-host-communities)).

A government tender closing 25 June 2026 commissions a National Digital Skills Assessment with framework development and an implementation plan ([tender](2026-06-25-expression-of-interest-for-conducting-national-digital-skills-assessment-framework-development-and-implementation-plan)).

The household assessment covers refugee and host-community sites only and is not nationally representative, which is why the tender exists.

summary: Computing is [an optional secondary subject the curriculum itself expects schools to lack facilities for](2013-01-01-curriculum-framework-south-sudan); a [mentorship scheme](2026-04-15-ttosict-stakeholder-kick-off-meeting) began in three schools.
developments:
The national curriculum places information and communications technology among the optional secondary subjects alongside Kiswahili, French, Arabic, arts and physical education, and states that many schools lacked facilities so the subject would run as a stand-alone catch-up programme where they were absent ([curriculum](2013-01-01-curriculum-framework-south-sudan)).

A stakeholder meeting at Juba Day Secondary School in April 2026 co-created an implementation plan for a mentorship programme across three selected secondary schools, run by a telecommunications union fellow with vendor support ([programme](2026-04-15-ttosict-stakeholder-kick-off-meeting)).

Three schools, and a curriculum that anticipated its own non-delivery thirteen years ago.

summary: A [new public university opened with computing programmes](2026-02-07-first-university-opens-in-bentiu-unity-state) in February 2026, extending qualifications beyond Juba.
developments:
The government's own admission guide confirms computer science and information technology as faculties or specialisations at the University of Juba, which runs a four-year bachelor's degree through its own school, and at two private university colleges ([guide](2025-03-01-admission-guide-for-institutions-of-higher-education-2024-2025)).

Bentiu University of Petroleum opened as Unity State's first public university with a bachelor's degree in computer science and a diploma in information technology approved among its initial programmes ([university](2026-02-07-first-university-opens-in-bentiu-unity-state)), and five public universities were equipped with twenty desktop computers and a projector each ([equipment](2025-10-22-undp-supports-five-public-universities-enhance-research-capacity-country)).

Twenty computers per university is the scale of the facilities behind the qualifications.

summary: Two [clause-level analyses](2026-02-01-digital-frontiers-and-legal-bounds-7-impactful-takeaways-from-south-sudans-new-cybercrime-act) of the 2026 statutes were published from outside government; no public research programme exists.
developments:
A regional information and communications technology policy think tank analysed the 2021 Cybercrimes and Computer Misuse Provisional Order, recommending court-order requirements for data access, enactment of a data protection law, ratification of the African Union convention and deletion of the offensive-communication provision ([analysis](2021-11-01-analysis-of-the-south-sudan-cybercrimes-and-computer-misuse-provisional-order-2021)).

A South Sudanese civil-society chapter published a clause-level breakdown of the Cybercrimes and Computer Misuse Act 2026 covering extraterritorial jurisdiction, 180-day data retention, content-moderation duties, critical infrastructure designation and new digital-harassment offences ([breakdown](2026-02-01-digital-frontiers-and-legal-bounds-7-impactful-takeaways-from-south-sudans-new-cybercrime-act)), and a digital rights research organisation argued for a genuinely independent and resourced data protection authority rather than a bill alone ([argument](2026-02-04-an-independent-data-protection-act-a-critical-part-to-south-sudans-digital-future)).

Every contribution on record is from outside government, and none is answered in a text.

summary: No digital channel: complaints run through the [statutory grievances chamber](2011-01-01-south-sudan-public-grievances-act) and, from April 2026, a [procurement complaints committee](2026-04-21-south-sudan-ppdaa-complaints-review-committee).
developments:
The Public Grievances Chamber is the statutory citizen complaints mechanism against government institutions ([Act](2011-01-01-south-sudan-public-grievances-act)).

The procurement authority operationalised a Complaints Review Committee in April 2026 as an independent administrative review route under the 2018 Procurement Act ([committee](2026-04-21-south-sudan-ppdaa-complaints-review-committee)), and three community peace desks were activated in Unity State to receive concerns and housing, land and property issues, against an assessment finding 35 per cent of respondents needing guidance on how to submit a complaint and 42 per cent withholding feedback for fear of reprisal ([desks](2026-01-29-south-sudan-aap-wg-peace-desks-meeting-summary)).

Every route on record is in person or on paper, and four in ten people will not use one.

summary: A [35 per cent quota and a gender policy stand above two bills that have not passed](2024-07-01-south-sudan-beijing30-national-review-report); two projects launched in the period.
developments:
The government's own review confirms the National Gender Policy, records the anti-gender-based-violence and family law bills as both introduced in 2023 and still bills, and states a 35 per cent quota for women in government under the revitalised peace agreement ([review](2024-07-01-south-sudan-beijing30-national-review-report)).

Two peacebuilding fund initiatives launched with the government in July 2026 reaching more than 8,000 women and young people, 2,100 of them women and girls, with leadership, livelihoods, digital empowerment and community dialogue ([initiatives](2026-07-31-south-sudan-unesco-iom-unwomen-peacebuilding-projects)), and a regional project launched in Torit in August 2026 linking women's economic empowerment to land rights and governance ([project](2026-08-18-south-sudan-igad-bwersp-women-economic-resilience)).

No sex-disaggregated figure for phone ownership, internet use or identity registration is published anywhere in the base.

summary: [1,400 teachers were trained in sign language and Braille](2025-10-08-south-sudan-ecw-inclusive-classrooms-sign-language-braille) across three national institutes, under a 2020 action plan.
developments:
The National Disability Action Plan implements the 2015 policy and sets interventions across data management, health care, rehabilitation, education and law ([plan](2020-01-01-south-sudan-national-disability-action-plan)).

An education emergency fund programme trained 1,400 teachers in sign language, Braille and inclusive pedagogy at three national teacher-training institutes over two years ([training](2025-10-08-south-sudan-ecw-inclusive-classrooms-sign-language-braille)), and a disability-inclusive food security training package was launched in Wau in July 2026 and in Juba later that month ([package](2026-08-21-south-sudan-hi-disability-inclusive-food-security-training)).

Both reach services rather than systems. No accessibility requirement attaches to any government digital service on record.

summary: A [US$67 million regional integration project](2025-08-29-south-sudan-eardip-implementation-support-mission) carries the connectivity programme, alongside a [2,400 kilometre backbone](2025-10-10-south-sudan-2400km-fibre-plan) and [solar power for 500 network sites](2026-02-19-south-sudan-eu-backed-green-telecom-expansion).
developments:
The regional digital integration project, at US$67 million, is the active programme addressing connectivity and the digital divide through broadband fibre deployment ([mission](2025-08-29-south-sudan-eardip-implementation-support-mission)).

The telecommunications undersecretary announced a 2,400 kilometre national backbone connecting to Kenya, intended to shift the country from expensive satellite connectivity toward terrestrial broadband reaching rural areas ([backbone](2025-10-10-south-sudan-2400km-fibre-plan)), and a follow-on US$5 million investment, US$10 million in total, financed solar-hybrid power for over 500 mobile network sites, improving reliability in areas without stable electricity ([power](2026-02-19-south-sudan-eu-backed-green-telecom-expansion)).

Every instrument here is external. None is financed domestically, and the usage divide they address is not measured.

summary: The [first strategy ran to 2020 on a US$58 million budget](2014-01-01-south-sudan-nsds-strategic-plan); a second is being built out through an [agricultural statistics plan](2026-05-12-south-sudan-fao-agricultural-statistics-diagnostic-workshop).
developments:
The bureau's first strategy, covering 2014 to 2020, set legal and institutional, human resource capacity, statistical infrastructure and data development objectives on a US$58 million budget ([strategy](2014-01-01-south-sudan-nsds-strategic-plan)).

The finance minister publicly committed government support to the bureau in January 2026, covering the second strategy, legal reform, sustainable financing and administrative data ([commitment](2026-01-22-south-sudan-govt-pledges-support-nbs)), and a five-day diagnostic workshop in May 2026 produced the foundation for a Strategic Plan for Agricultural and Rural Statistics for 2026 to 2031 aligned to it ([workshop](2026-05-12-south-sudan-fao-agricultural-statistics-diagnostic-workshop)).

The second strategy's own text is not held. Six years after the first expired, what the base shows is work aligned to a document it cannot read.

summary: Health is the only sector publishing from administrative data - a [statistical abstract of about ninety tables](2025-01-01-south-sudan-2025-health-statistics-abstract) built on the national instance.
developments:
The abstract covers health status, risk factors, service coverage and health systems indicators across about ninety tables, built on administrative health data ([abstract](2025-01-01-south-sudan-2025-health-statistics-abstract)).

The health agency's 2025 annual report, organised by quarter and cluster, covers strengthened health information systems and administrative-data reporting alongside emergency response and primary health care ([report](2026-02-01-south-sudan-who-annual-report-2025)).

No other sector publishes a statistical product from its own administrative records, and the education, land and justice systems recorded separately have no data to publish from.

summary: The [first nationally representative household dataset since independence](2026-04-21-south-sudan-mics7-national-survey-released) was released in April 2026, alongside a [public food security dashboard](2026-05-09-south-sudan-climis-ipc-population-dashboard).
developments:
The statistics bureau and a United Nations agency released the 2025 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey publicly with full results and detailed data ([survey](2026-04-21-south-sudan-mics7-national-survey-released)).

The food security information system's public dashboard lets users query state-level phase populations for April to July 2026, turning a major humanitarian assessment into queryable data ([dashboard](2026-05-09-south-sudan-climis-ipc-population-dashboard)), and the bureau runs an open data portal on public, registered and restricted tiers ([portal](2026-08-29-south-sudan-nbs-open-data-portal)).

Fifteen years to a first national household dataset. Everything open in this base is statistical, and no policy requires any of it.

summary: Satellite-derived flood mapping carried the [April 2026 outlook projecting Emergency across 34 counties](2026-04-30-south-sudan-fews-net-april-2026-outlook) and a famine risk in four.
developments:
The national crop assessment triangulates field task force work and county crop monitoring committees with satellite-derived vegetation index and rainfall data from two United Nations agencies ([assessment](2026-03-19-south-sudan-cfsam-2025)).

The April 2026 food security outlook used satellite-derived flood extent mapping alongside rainfall and crop condition data to project Emergency outcomes across 34 counties and a credible risk of Famine in four through September 2026 ([outlook](2026-04-30-south-sudan-fews-net-april-2026-outlook)), and a monthly monitor combines vegetation index and rainfall with conflict, price and exchange-rate data across the 78 second-level administrative areas ([monitor](2025-10-20-south-sudan-joint-food-security-monitor)).

Every product is produced by an external agency. No national earth-observation capability appears in the base.

summary: The observation network went from [three manual stations](2025-07-16-south-sudan-crews-east-africa-twinning) to [forty automatic ones sharing data internationally](2026-02-12-south-sudan-27-new-automatic-weather-stations).
developments:
The meteorological service had three manual observation stations covering a country larger than Kenya, with forecasters newly trained to use satellite data and global numerical weather prediction outputs ([capacity](2025-07-16-south-sudan-crews-east-africa-twinning)).

Twenty-seven further automatic weather stations were installed, bringing the total to forty sharing data on the global information system towards basic observing network compliance ([stations](2026-02-12-south-sudan-27-new-automatic-weather-stations)), and a US$2,079,598.80 investment funding request was approved in February 2026 for surface observing stations, maintenance, data and information technology systems and staff training ([funding](2026-02-19-south-sudan-soff-investment-funding-decision)).

A thirteen-fold increase in stations inside a year, entirely externally financed.

summary: [EUR 304 million was allocated 2021-2024](2025-09-30-south-sudan-eu-international-partnerships-page) under the programming framework, with no digital instrument named within it.
developments:
The partnership runs under the 2021-2027 programming framework and the Global Gateway strategy, with EUR 304 million allocated between 2021 and 2024 across agri-food systems, jobs and education, health, migration and governance ([partnership](2025-09-30-south-sudan-eu-international-partnerships-page)).

A further EUR 35 million of humanitarian funding was allocated in November 2025 within a EUR 143 million sub-Saharan package ([humanitarian](2025-11-24-south-sudan-eu-143m-humanitarian-response)), and the Council reviewed and maintained the restrictive-measures listing of a serving minister in June 2026, updating it to reflect his move to the justice portfolio ([sanctions](2026-06-22-south-sudan-eu-sanctions-regulation-2026-1402)).

Development money and a sanctions listing running at once. No digital-sector instrument is named in either.

summary: The legislature [ratified the Saudi cooperation agreement](2026-08-19-south-sudan-tnla-ratifies-saudi-cooperation-agreement) in August 2026, having rejected it three months earlier on sovereignty grounds.
developments:
Four founding instruments with the United Arab Emirates - mutual investment protection, avoidance of double taxation, visa waivers and technical cooperation on training diplomats - were signed on 24 April 2019 ([instruments](2019-04-24-south-sudan-uae-mous-signing)).

The legislature ratified the general cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia signed in 2022, covering agriculture, education, mining, infrastructure, health, trade, investment, security and social development, after rejecting it in May 2026 on sovereignty grounds ([ratification](2026-08-19-south-sudan-tnla-ratifies-saudi-cooperation-agreement)); the UAE aid agency signed an US$11 million agreement with the Red Cross federation in January 2026, US$10 million of it for refugee-hosting communities across four countries including South Sudan ([agreement](2026-01-18-south-sudan-uae-ifrc-11m-humanitarian-agreement)).

No digital or data commitment appears in any of them.

summary: The [first Foreign Office Consultations](2025-12-05-south-sudan-india-first-foreign-office-consultations) were held in December 2025, six years after the memorandum providing for them.
developments:
India's bilateral brief consolidates the 2019 consultations memorandum, a December 2025 framework agreement, the first consultations round and a research association concluded in April 2026 between a Juba institute and an Indian research body ([brief](2026-04-12-south-sudan-india-bilateral-relations-brief)).

The consultations were held in Juba on 4 December 2025, reviewing capacity building, health, technical and vocational training, trade and people-to-people relations, with a second round agreed for New Delhi ([consultations](2025-12-05-south-sudan-india-first-foreign-office-consultations)), and a technical and vocational education partnership was launched with UNESCO and the education ministry on 31 October 2025 ([partnership](2025-11-07-south-sudan-india-unesco-tvet-initiative)).

Capacity building and training throughout. No digital agreement, financing or technology transfer is named on either side.
